title: Weekly Dose of Optimism #217
gist: Packy McCormick's Weekly Dose #217 covers OpenAI's claimed AI proofs (including refuting the Exponential Time Hypothesis) shared via expert 'shepherds', Anthropic's preclinical drug-development programs (89% faster manufacturing review, a Mithril Medicine acquisition), and Lilly's retatrutide hitting sleep apnea endpoints (34 fewer events per hour). Also Neuralink VOICE at 75 wpm for an ALS patient and Anduril's BlueChip computer.

insights.claim: OpenAI announced AI-generated results in harmonic analysis (a proof of the local smoothing conjecture in every dimension, which would also settle Kakeya), complexity theory (a refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis) and quantum field theory (a proof that interacting QFTs including Yang-Mills exist in four dimensions, described as half of a Millennium Prize problem).
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: If the results survive expert review, frontier labs are moving from benchmark claims to verifiable research output, strengthening the case for compute and model spend; if they fail review, it is a credibility hit.
insights.quote: In computer science, a model refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH)
insights.locator: (2) OpenAI Says Its Models Disproved the ETH

insights.claim: OpenAI changed its rollout after the earlier episode in which GPT-5 'solved' ten Erdos problems that were mostly already in the literature: it now shares outputs with unpaid, NDA-free expert 'shepherds' who decide whether and where to publish, and some groups (the physics group) withhold the AI material and write it up themselves.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Credibility of AI science claims now depends on third-party expert validation, so watch which named experts endorse or reject these results before treating them as real.
insights.locator: (2) OpenAI Says Its Models Disproved the ETH

insights.claim: Lean formal verification does not fully close the trust gap: it guarantees the proof proves the formal statement, but human experts must still confirm the formal statement is the right one.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: The residual bottleneck in AI math is statement-checking by humans, which limits how fast verified results can scale.
insights.quote: human shepherds still have to confirm that the formal statement is the right one
insights.locator: (2) OpenAI Says Its Models Disproved the ETH

insights.claim: Axiom announced a complete Lean auto-formalization of the Classification of Finite Simple Groups (~15,000 pages, 100+ mathematicians, never fully checked by one person), while Georges Gonthier's team needed six years in 2012 for just the Feit-Thompson piece; Physical Superintelligence also released five Lean-formalized solutions to open quantum problems.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Formalization throughput is itself a scarce capability that AI-math neolabs are selling, needed to keep pace with the lab output.
insights.quote: Axiom announced a complete Lean auto-formalization of the Classification of Finite Simple Groups
insights.locator: (2) OpenAI Says Its Models Disproved the ETH

themes.theme: AI across the drug development pipeline

insights.claim: Anthropic argues that AI drug discovery focuses on finding molecules while the real bottlenecks are downstream, and that development is a whole-system problem where any un-accelerated step slows everything; its life sciences team therefore partnered with six organizations and runs programs itself.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Value may accrue to players who compress the full development chain (regulatory, manufacturing, trial design) rather than molecule generators alone.
insights.quote: you have to improve the whole thing at once, lest any one thing that didn’t improve slows the whole thing down
insights.locator: (2a) Anthropic Publishes Progress on Accelerating Drug Development

insights.claim: Reported preclinical wins: Divergence Labs' Claude-generated ~35,000 antibody designs in a month yielded three early hits that dislodged IgE better than the standard drug; Generate Biomedicines got a CAR-T design ~70% shorter producing ~10x as many receptors; BigHat tested ~1,010 variants in 10 weeks with best binding over 10x tighter.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Vendor-reported and preclinical only; the speedup is in design-test cycle time, not yet in clinical outcomes.
insights.quote: Anthropic is upfront that nearly all of this is preclinical
insights.locator: (2a) Anthropic Publishes Progress on Accelerating Drug Development

insights.claim: On the paperwork side, Claude reviewed 1,061 pages of Enveda manufacturing records, caught all human-found issues plus seven missed, cut review time by 89%, and drafted a regulatory document in four hours versus about three months by hand; manufacturing scientists there spend up to 75% of time on documentation.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Regulatory and QA documentation is a near-term, lower-risk monetizable AI use case in biotech than discovery.
insights.locator: (2a) Anthropic Publishes Progress on Accelerating Drug Development

insights.claim: The Column Group is launching Pleiades to run many more drug programs with Claude than a small team normally could, on the theory that cheaper, faster discovery lets investors back riskier ideas; Bristol Myers Squibb is using Claude to estimate early-stage drug success odds.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: If AI lowers per-program cost, biotech venture could shift toward portfolios of many cheap shots, changing risk appetite and fund structures.
insights.quote: if discovery gets cheaper and faster, investors can back riskier ideas
insights.locator: (2a) Anthropic Publishes Progress on Accelerating Drug Development

insights.claim: Anthropic acquired one-person biotech Mithril Medicine in July; founder Cody Tranbarger used Claude to run experiments across 11 outside labs and took a rare muscular dystrophy treatment from idea to promising mouse results in under 18 months, with human trials possible as soon as late 2028.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Signals a model of AI-orchestrated, outsourced-lab biotech where tiny teams run full programs; also shows Anthropic moving into owning programs, not only selling tools.
insights.locator: (2a) Anthropic Publishes Progress on Accelerating Drug Development

insights.claim: An AI agent given 19 gene therapy vectors, an epilepsy mouse model and a motorized surgery rig reportedly chose the drug and brain region and performed brain surgery on a mouse with the goal of reducing seizures.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Agentic control of physical lab workflows is emerging, but this is a single tweet-thread claim the author had not vetted.
insights.quote: I just saw this one this morning, so didn’t have time to write it up
insights.locator: (2b) Robot + Agent Perform Brain Surgery on Mouse

insights.claim: Lilly's retatrutide (GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triple agonist) cut sleep apnea events by 34 per hour at 9 mg versus 10 on placebo in the non-diabetic trial, with about half of higher-dose patients reaching resolved or mild apnea versus roughly one in ten on placebo, in two 80-week Phase 3 trials of 691 adults starting at ~57 events per hour.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A sleep apnea label would compete directly with CPAP and expand the addressable market of tens of millions of mostly undiagnosed patients.
insights.locator: (4) Reta Works on Sleep Apnea, Too

insights.claim: Retatrutide's accumulating evidence spans multiple indications: 28.3% weight loss over 80 weeks (TRIUMPH-1), 75-83% reaching A1C of 6.5% or lower (TRANSCEND-T2D-1), 22.6% weight loss with hsCRP down 51% in heart disease patients (TRIUMPH-3), knee pain down about three-quarters, and 93% with normal liver fat in Phase 2.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Breadth of benefit supports a multi-indication, pricing-power thesis for Lilly, with the cardiorenal outcomes trial the key remaining catalyst.
insights.quote: a drug that cuts weight, lowers heart disease risk, fights diabetes, cuts liver fat, makes our knees feel better, and replaces a CPAP
insights.locator: (4) Reta Works on Sleep Apnea, Too

insights.claim: Lilly reportedly crushed earnings this week and raised its full-year revenue outlook by $5 billion; the author says it deserves its $1.3T market cap, while an open question remains whether retatrutide's improvements prevent heart attack and stroke, which Lilly's dedicated cardiorenal trial will test.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A positive cardiorenal readout is the upside catalyst; a miss would test a $1.3T valuation priced on broad benefit.
insights.quote: deserves every dollar of its $1.3T market cap
insights.locator: (4) Reta Works on Sleep Apnea, Too

insights.claim: Neuralink's VOICE reached 75 words per minute with a 5.8% error rate on a 125,000-word vocabulary in one ALS participant's first week, versus Stanford's 2023 system at 62 wpm with nearly a quarter of words wrong; natural speech is about 160 wpm, and the system can use the participant's pre-ALS voice.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Single-participant data in a trial planned for up to six people with Breakthrough Device designation; sample size caps confidence but the trajectory beats prior published work.
insights.quote: 75 words per minute with a 5.8% error rate across a 125,000 word vocabulary
insights.locator: (5) Neuralink Gives Voice Back to ALS Patients

insights.claim: Elon Musk said Neuralink's second product, Blindsight, is ready from an engineering standpoint and is waiting only on regulatory approval, and that Telepathy output bandwidth will vastly exceed fastest human speech or typing in a few years.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Regulatory approval, not engineering, is the stated gating item; treat timelines from Musk as promotional until the FDA acts.
insights.locator: (5) Neuralink Gives Voice Back to ALS Patients

insights.claim: Anduril announced BlueChip, a Made-in-America computer using American-sourced components, metals and batteries; the author reads this as Anduril having built a machine that can make machines, where enough engineers, capital, manufacturing and distribution let it build almost anything, in the mold of Elon's companies.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Anduril is extending from defense hardware into consumer-scale electronics and supply chain, a vertical-integration play worth tracking as a platform rather than a single-product company.
insights.quote: it seems as if Anduril has gotten to the point where it’s built a machine that can make machines

insights.claim: High-volume products like laptops can create the demand pull to reshore more of the supply chain, because unit volume justifies domestic mining, refining and component capacity.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Consumer-scale volume, not defense procurement alone, may be what makes domestic supply chains economic.
insights.quote: making products that can sell a ton of units, like laptops, can create the pull to bring more of the supply chain here

insights.claim: The issue's extra doses flag DoorDash acquiring Instacart and Thrive Holdings acquiring ADT, but the details are behind the paywall in this excerpt.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Only headlines are visible; verify before relying on these as completed or confirmed deals.
insights.quote: EXTRA DOSES: The Commanding Heights, Science Breakthroughs, DoorDash Acquires Instacart, Thrive Holdings Acquires ADT, LIFE

insights.claim: Readwise Books, a Kindle-meets-Goodreads reader with Strava-like leaderboards, native AI, highlight sync and text-to-speech, is the author's second-most-used phone app; the author discloses being an investor and friend of the founders.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Biased endorsement from an investor; shows gamified reading as a retention mechanic.
